evidence:
Priya has the order invoice, the seller's tax invoice, the product listing screenshot showing the warranty and replacement terms, and the delivery confirmation with a timestamp. She took an unboxing video on delivery day that shows the box dent but also a working screen on first power-on, which is helpful for her. She has photos of the screen showing the vertical line and the later complete failure, with file timestamps that match her account. The platform's chat transcripts and her email threads show a pattern of being passed between parties, with the platform's agent at one point writing that "the seller will resolve this."

The technician's service report states "physical damage suspected, warranty void" but includes no photographs, no inspection checklist, and no description of visible impact marks. Priya has no independent expert opinion yet. The warranty card was not in the box, and the brand's website says the warranty is registered automatically on purchase, a claim she has not been able to confirm. There is no evidence of any drop or mishandling, although the delivery courier's handover photo shows the box being carried loosely.

events.description: Priya Menon bought a 55-inch smart TV for 62,000 from an online marketplace during a "festival sale," selling through a third-party seller.
The listing stated "1-year brand warranty + 7-day replacement." The TV arrived with a minor box dent but worked for 19 days.
On day 20, a vertical line appeared on the screen, followed by complete panel failure a week later.
She raised a complaint on the platform, which routed her to the seller, who said the panel damage was "physical" and not covered.
The brand's service center sent a technician who, after a brief visit, marked the issue as "customer damage, warranty void" without opening the device.
Priya argues the damage is a manufacturing defect that appeared within the warranty, and that the seller and the platform both owe her a remedy.
The seller says the 7-day replacement window has lapsed, the brand says warranty is void, and the platform says it is only an intermediary.
Priya has spent six weeks on calls and chats, receiving contradictory responses from each party.
She now wants a refund or replacement, plus compensation for the harassment, and asks who is actually legally responsible and which forum she should go to.

follow_up.why: The response can show what the seller disputes or offered.

evidence_plan.heading: Evidence plan
prompts: Which part of the timeline needs independent support?
What already shows that event, and who may lawfully hold another record?

suggestions.title: Purchase, promised terms and communications
suggestions.look_for: Look for the order confirmation, invoice, payment record and relevant warranty or service terms. Keep the complete email or chat thread.
suggestions.why: These can show what was purchased, what was promised and what resolution the seller offered.
suggestions.action: Keep the original files or exports. Record dates and ask for copies from the seller or platform if you do not have them.

suggestions.title: Condition of the product or work
suggestions.look_for: If safe, note the model or order number, the fault and when it appeared. Keep existing dated photos, service requests or repair reports.
suggestions.why: A dated record helps distinguish what you observed from a possible explanation of the fault.
suggestions.action: Leave suspected electrical or other hazardous damage to a qualified person. Ask the repair provider for a written report if they inspect it.

suggestions.title: Original records and an evidence log
suggestions.look_for: Keep records you lawfully have, with their surrounding context. For each item note the related event, who provided it, when you received it, and any transfer.
suggestions.why: The log distinguishes what you observed from what someone later told you and makes it easier to check the source.
suggestions.action: Keep an unchanged original and label working copies. Avoid editing originals, guessing gaps, or sharing evidence publicly.

suggestions.title: Maruti Udyog Ltd. v. Susheel Kumar Gabgotra
suggestions.takeaway: For the particular car warranty and defect, the Court ordered free replacement of the defective clutch assembly and a payment for specified expenses and inconvenience instead of replacement of the whole car.
suggestions.difference: The Court applied the former Jammu and Kashmir consumer law and a specific vehicle warranty. Your options depend on the applicable law, warranty, evidence and remedy requested.
suggestions.connection: Your account describes an alleged problem with a purchased product.
suggestions.preparation: Put the invoice, warranty, repair offers and any inspection findings together. Explain why your requested remedy fits the problem.

route.title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 · Section 35
route.details: Section 35 sets out who can make a complaint to the District Commission and permits electronic filing. Check the proper commission, time limits and required documents for your situation.
